answer: Anchor each agent's identity to a verifiable stake, such as a small refundable deposit or a history of useful work, so creating many fake identities becomes costly. Let the reputation pool act like a lagoon: new agents enter slowly through a shallow channel, earning trust gradually instead of flooding in at once. Agents that behave honestly build an oasis of reliable counterparties they can trade with, while sybils stranded outside that trusted network find no one willing to transact. Costly entry plus slow trust makes mass forgery unprofitable.
